frontier.hypothesis: There may exist a moved movable that costs zero emitted bytes. H22 prices one at 3 counted insns, so 18 of them close the entire remaining deficit - this is now the highest-leverage unknown in the ledger.
frontier.mechanism: A movable is hoisted into the preheader, so it is free iff its preheader insn disappears afterwards. Two mechanisms could do that and neither has been measured: (a) the hoisted def becomes DEAD because its in-loop use is erased after loop_optimize by combine's force_to_mode (tools/gcc-2.7.2/combine.c:5682) - i.e. s14's channel applied to an INVARIANT rather than a variant local; note K44 shows the naive constant-xor spelling folds at cse1, so the carrier must be non-foldable (distinct operators, or a value cse1 cannot constant-fold); (b) the hoisted def is COALESCED into an existing preheader insn by regmove or local-alloc.
frontier.next_probe: Build one invariant carrier of each shape with tmp/grind/func_8003C714/s15/{mk.py,sweep.sh}, read the .seg dump for a fourth 'moved to' line, and read asm_lines for the byte cost. A shape measuring +1 counted insn, +1 moved movable and 107 asm lines is decisive. If every shape that is free is also inert, that is the strong citable statement that the two-term budget cannot be paid in ordinary C - which is exactly what an eventual foreclosure record would have to establish.

frontier.hypothesis: s1's H2 - that the entire 15-instruction residual is the 0x91A2B3C5 const placement plus the mfhi-temp seat - has never been re-verified in fourteen sessions and is the weakest verdict in the ledger under the CONTRADICTION RULE, because it is the single assumption that makes the loop.c hoist the only thing worth attacking.
frontier.mechanism: If any of the 15 differing instructions is independent of the const placement, it is separately closable and the s15-E budget is not the only front; if all 15 really are downstream of the hoist, the budget is the whole problem and the frontier collapses to item 1.
frontier.next_probe: Apply the s_max body (rejected/splitinit-ceiling-63-ordinary-c-byte-neutral-but-54-short.c), run pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8003C714, and diff the .greg / .sched output against asm/funcs/func_8003C714.s instruction by instruction, classifying each of the 15 as const-placement-dependent or not.

frontier.hypothesis: The two declaration puns flagged by the brief's auto-scan remain a hard submission blocker on ANY distance-0 body, independent of the floor.
frontier.mechanism: candidate.c:342 'src = (u8 *)&D_80106A58 + i * 8;' uses a per-word splat sub-symbol of g_file_disc_type @80106A54, and candidate.c:354 '*((u8 *)s0 + 0x30) = *(u16 *)&D_80101ED2;' reads an s16-declared symbol through a pun. The sanctioned fix is the aggregate-merge family at the DECLARATION in include/*.h via an integration handoff, prongs (a)-(e), with prong (c)'s 2026-09-03 amendment requiring the sub-symbol rows to carry an 'alias of g_file_disc_type+4; retire with func_80035280' suffix because func_80035280 is still INCLUDE_ASM. A per-use cast is an auto-FAIL.
frontier.next_probe: Prong (a) looks satisfiable from base-register/stride evidence rather than the forbidden adjacency-of-splat-names evidence: the target's loop walks a single base register $a2 with 'addiu $a2, $a2, 0x8' at 8003C830. Draft the header-canonical merged declaration and route it as an integration handoff before any candidate-ready.
